purpose: Agent-readable artifact, approval and submission contract for the R3.0-009 unified semantic graph and commonality abstraction flow. It extends the R3.0-008B staged decisions contract in place: same run root, same seven-gate order, same Runner-private submission capability, plus the versioned 009 candidate, coordinator decisions, translation approvals, materialization plan and the 009 intent/receipt bindings. It is only in force for a Team Task that declares parameters.unified_semantic_graph: true; 008B tasks keep their own schemas and are never re-validated against this contract.

task_parameter.name: unified_semantic_graph
task_parameter.rule: The parameter is declared on the v2 Task only. Turning it on inside an existing run to skip a gate is forbidden; a run keeps the schema it started with.

schema_dispatch.rule: Readers and writers dispatch on the recorded schema_version of each artifact together with the Task mode. 008B mode writes and validates only the r3-0-008b v1 schemas; 009 mode writes the schemas listed here. A schema/mode mismatch is a typed, fixable error, never a silent downgrade. Historical evidence is validated with the schema it records; an old intent/receipt is never retro-fitted with 009 bindings.

artifact_locations.note: Run-workspace process artifacts, not platform storage. The candidates/ and materialization-plans/ directories are prepared by the Runner at prepare time; files are created only by their single writer and are never pre-created.

directory_writers.read_visibility: Only the unique writer of each directory receives a writable bind; candidates/ and materialization-plans/ are bound separately from the Modeling-only stage3 root so Protocol and the Runner can read the published plan without gaining write access to Modeling artifacts.

rules: candidate_contract replaces the 008B deferred_contract and must name r3-0-009-unified-graph/v1
candidate_artifacts lists the published candidate files this slot approves
Modeling writes the slot; the Coordinator confirms it inside the approvals artifact
items are neutral: no guessed platform IRI, semantic ID, or receipt reference
candidate_id plus revision is immutable once published; a change publishes a new revision file and requires new approvals

a candidate item carries exactly item_fields and nothing else; the set is closed and a submission validates it, so an item carrying any extra field such as scope is rejected as unified_schema_mismatch (candidate item fields drift from the contract)

shared_scope is the only item-level commonality carrier: a short non-empty string label on commonality relations, empty/null on every other item; scope is a Coordinator decision field (a non-empty JSON object mandatory on commonality_relation decisions, null on every other decision) and never appears on a candidate item - authoring the decision's scope mapping onto the item duplicates approved decision content and drifts the item from the closed field set

approvals.entry_rule: entries keeps the 008B conclusion_confirmation/stage3_slot entries, their fields and their validation, unchanged and unmixed with the new kinds.
rules: the Coordinator is the only writer; only an approved current decision releases a translation
scope is mandatory for commonality_relation decisions as a non-empty JSON object (a mapping of scope names to values, never an array or a plain string) and must stay null everywhere else
every decision carries at least one evidence_ref and the content_digest of the exact candidate content it approves
a translation approval proves one plan_ref/projection_digest pair, not a mutable file name

R3.0-014: translation_approvals never gate a dry-run. Empty, old-plan, rejected or format-drifted entries are history: only the list shape itself is validated up front, and the exact-key match is evaluated at apply time only

R3.0-014: an apply additionally requires one current translation approval keyed exactly to the submitted (plan_ref, projection_digest) whose approved_by is the run's current Coordinator role ID. Equivalent repeats (same key, approver and decision) count as one decision; a genuine decision or approver conflict on the same key is approval_conflict

R3.0-014: approvals are a keyed read-modify-write surface — the Coordinator re-reads the current artifact and appends its (plan_ref, projection_digest)-keyed entry instead of rewriting history, so concurrent reviewers never erase each other's decisions

projection.task_id is a caller-supplied authoring identifier copied verbatim from the frozen Task snapshot's own task_id field; it is never expected from any platform read (get_project_build_context, get_build_session and related reads do not return it), and substituting a placeholder, an empty value or the run_id for it is a plan-authoring violation, not a missing authority value

projection.session_id is the actual Build Session identifier of this run's accepted Build Session (the exact value the submission forwards as batch.session_id); it is never the run_id or scenario id, and authoring a projection with any other value is a plan-authoring violation that the submission-time projection rebuild rejects as approval_content_mismatch

projection items carry competency_question_ids exactly as the batch item contract requires: empty unless the platform project actually contains those CompetencyQuestion rows; the R3.0-011 question pool is a run artifact and never a platform resource, so putting pool IDs into a projection is a plan-authoring violation that fails closed at submission with competency_question_not_found findings

projection items carry depends_on exactly as the batch item contract requires: every entry names a client_item_id inside the same plan's projection, because the platform resolves dependencies against the current batch only; cross-plan ordering lives in the recorded submission order and never in depends_on, and a cross-plan entry fails closed as invalid_dependency
projection items are the full ModelingItemInput projection including omitted defaults, so the digest covers exactly what is forwarded
every forwarded item is bound to candidate content through a decision binding, including items with no commonality decision

candidate_content_digests is a JSON object mapping candidate item_id to that item's canonical digest, never an array of digests; a non-object shape is a typed unified_schema_mismatch naming the field, so the plan is rejected at load time instead of failing inside a close check
identity bindings carry exactly one of resource_iri (with the approved read evidence_ref) and receipt_ref; a future IRI is never fabricated
execution parameters (lease, mode, idempotency key, expected workspace version) never enter the projection or its digest

digest_rules.canonical_json: UTF-8 json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')) hashed with SHA-256 and prefixed with sha256:
digest_rules.self_exclusion: a digest field is never part of the value it digests
digest_rules.class_iris: legacy Class IDs are expanded first; class_iris is then deduplicated and sorted by IRI, so input order never changes a digest. All other arrays keep submission order.
digest_rules.candidate_item_digest: canonical JSON digest of the complete published candidate item object
digest_rules.candidate_digest: canonical JSON digest of the candidate's items list in published order
digest_rules.projection_digest: canonical JSON digest of the whole projection object; projection carries no digest field of its own

submission_capability.plan_ref_rule: In 009 mode plan_ref is mandatory, must be a run-relative path under stage3-neutral-graph/materialization-plans/, and must not be a symlink or escape the run root.
acceptance_timing: before the request is accepted the current plan is re-read, the approved projection is rebuilt from the payloads actually being forwarded and compared field by field; a self-reported digest never substitutes for matching content

the projection is then closed against the currently published candidate revision and against the current approved decisions; any drift returns approval_stale or approval_content_mismatch without a partial write
once the comparison passes, the captured projection is frozen: durable intent and forwarder use that in-memory snapshot only and never re-read a role-writable path
the intent is written before forwarding; if saving fails, nothing is forwarded and a retry re-checks the current approval

R3.0-014: the staged order is dry-run first. A dry_run submission clears the three close checks above and is forwarded without consulting translation_approvals; technical findings come back on the attempt and are answered by fixing the plan and re-running the dry-run

R3.0-014: an apply_atomic submission is additionally gated, in order, on (a) the current-plan translation approval recorded by the run's current Coordinator (approval_missing/approval_conflict) and (b) a Runner-recorded validated dry-run Attempt proof of the same immutable content hash at the submitted workspace timepoint (dry_run_proof_missing/dry_run_proof_not_validated/dry_run_proof_content_mismatch/dry_run_proof_workspace_mismatch); reusing a dry-run idempotency key is idempotency_conflict

R3.0-014: the proof is Runner-owned host evidence (r3-0-014-attempt-proof/v1, event submission-attempt-proof-written). It is written only when the platform reply carries a complete read-back-verified Attempt identity (batch_id, attempt_id, mode, attempt_status, content_hash); a result without one yields no proof, so the apply gate fails closed on the missing record
R3.0-014: the capability response passes the Attempt facts through verbatim — mode, attempt_id, attempt_status, content_hash and findings — while ok states only that the receipt was written
submission_capability.isolation: plan_ref, projection, projection_digest and decision_bindings are Runner-private sidecar fields. They are never added to the platform ModelingItemInput payload, which forbids extra fields, and never leave the Runner sandbox.

rules: the association targets the Modeling Item a receipt or read-back named (target_id), never a candidate revision id or an invented identifier
this capability is out of the plan/approval chain: it mints no intent, consults no projection, and cannot unlock or re-open a materialization
it is the read-side complement of submission_capability: it closes the lineage gate of an item the staged write created, and it is idempotent per (target, evidence reference)
the receipt copies plan_ref, projection_digest and decision_bindings from the saved intent; it never rebuilds them
a 009 receipt whose projection_digest or plan_ref drifts from its intent is a kill-switch trigger
an old 008B intent/receipt only proves the old contract and never unlocks a 009 write
unknown results follow the existing idempotency/Batch reconciliation using the saved intent's approved version
a canonical read model row is identified by its own semantic_id, entity IRI and /vocab/id anchor; a formal Class is optional
each visible asserted type edge is verified independently; a Class never becomes an existence condition
a Class IRI whose own identity metadata is missing stays readable and is reported as incomplete_class_identity, never as confirmed no-class
a ref that expects no Class binds only a genuinely unclassified row; a row that still carries Class identity cannot satisfy it
the R2.3-003 class-first contract is unchanged and is not relaxed by this contract

forbidden: starting real modeling or applying production data under this contract alone
writing business rows as RDF individuals
auto-clustering, inheritance or any abstraction scoring engine
extending read authorization with candidate or approval evidence
modifying modeling_team/r23003_contract.py or the backend ModelingItemInput schema
